reviews.title: No Free Option Available
reviews.text: I wouldn’t get this app unless you want to pay $7.99 per WEEK for a food tracking app. The app waits for you to submit all your personal information, and then lets you know that your only option to use this app is to start a 3 Day Free Trial, and then $7.99 a week following. In the ‘fine print’ it also specifies that you much cancel this forced 3 day trial at least 24 hours prior to the end of your trial. So basically, you actually have a 48 hour free trial. There’s no way that they don’t pay for those AI bots that leave fake reviews to boost their ratings. I can’t convince myself that this app has actually been given a real overall 4 star rating. They would get a lot more long term users if they offered a free version. I do like the design and functionality of this app. But I’m not going to pay over $30 a month for this app when there’s plenty more affordable (and even free) options that offer the same features in a different style. I would rather take the time to monitor my progress, weight, and nutrients/cal intake on pencil and paper before I would pay $30 a month for this product. This company seems greedy and untrustworthy. I was immediately turned off by it, canceled the forced trial, and deleted the app. I know that it was likely some ‘big-wig’ in the company that decided on the price of the subscription. But to the average consumer, 30 something dollars every month for this subscription and what it offers is quite hefty. Yikes !

reviews.title: Honestly Like My Fitness Pal More
reviews.text:
I wanted to try out this tracker to see if there was a cheaper alternative to the $20 a month My Fitness Pal app. I wish I never switched, but I got roped into a year long subscription with this app.

I meal prep weekly. One feature I like in My Fitness Pal is that when you enter in all the ingredients you use in a recipe, it factors the macros automatically according to the number of servings you enter for that recipe. This app does NOT do this. In this app, you enter in your recipe and then there is no way to enter in the number of servings for the app to automatically factor the macros for a serving of said recipe. If you put say, your overnight oats recipe that makes 4 serving under your breakfast, it just puts all 4 servings there. And you can’t just put that you ate 1/4 of that recipe because they only allow 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 quantities. No .25, which is crazy to me. So then, you have to take out your calculator, pull up the recipe, and do the math on all your macros per serving yourself and then MANUALLY enter in the meal.

I’m only 1 meal into my prep and this app has already made it more difficult than it should be.

reviews.title: Hate the new update
reviews.text: The complete change in every aspect of the interface is a huge turn-off for me. The old UI had all the info I needed to see at a glance. This new one is so much harder to interpret. And it makes me add things one by one instead of in a group. I also hate the new “meal” pictures. They look cartoonish, and don’t even represent the kind of foods I’m trying to eat more of. It’s only been one day since my app updated, and I’m already resisting the idea of adding things to keep track of calories. I really wish I could revert back to the clean, minimalist style from before the update. I didn’t ask for any of these changes, and now I wish I didn’t have 10 months left on my paid subscription, because I probably won’t use this anymore.
